The financial note gives American Express 5,180m, Coca-Cola 13,400m and Gillette 4,590m. The letter common-stock list totals 37,265m and itemizes every position over 750m; S is 38,121m. The 856m difference is not silently discarded. The letter notes that the Cologne Re equity portfolio is not managed by Buffett/Munger.

Even assigning the entire 856m difference to Freddie Mac, the next-largest other named company, yields 3,885m + 856m = 4,741m, below American Express 5,180m. Any unlisted letter company is bounded by 750m + 856m = 1,606m. Thus second place is established in the financial S scope.

Third place is left null: the same 4,741m Freddie Mac upper bound exceeds financial-note Gillette 4,590m. Gillette is the disclosed candidate but the 856m outside the letter list is not decomposed by issuer.
